sources.text:
In the present study, a one-shot case study which is a pre-experimental design has been administered.

A total of 11 students from different departments with an English language level above B1 were included in this study on a voluntary basis.

According to the lesson plan, a writing lesson was held with the participants via Google Meet for 2 weeks, with two weekly lessons consisting of 50 min.

ChatGPT was perceived as more beneficial for formal text corrections. It was criticized for making changes without providing explanations. Students felt that ChatGPT focused more on grammar and punctuation than vocabulary.

Furthermore, the length and scope of the study might not have permitted a thorough assessment of the long-term impacts of ChatGPT use on writing development.

cases.rationale: This is the same source-supported claim as sample_duration_supported, but the selected span concerns unexplained revisions and students' views about grammar and punctuation. It supplies neither the participant count nor the lesson duration.

sources.text:
We analyzed secondary task performance in the conditions in which participants responded to the N-back task.

We observed a higher sensitivity in the no lockout than lockout condition, t(84) = −2.60, p = .011, ηp² = .07, 95% CI [.01, .19] (see Fig. 3).

Regarding response time, there was no difference between these conditions, t(84) = 1.27, p = .206, ηp² = .02, 95% CI [.00, .11].

The auditory stimuli for the secondary task (N-back task) were presented via headphones, and a foot pedal served as an input device for this task.

cases.rationale: The Results attach .011 to sensitivity and .206 to response time. The anchor includes the sensitivity p value and introduces the response-time comparison, which the next span completes. This claim reports the tests, not effect magnitudes.

cases.text: N-back sensitivity was higher without a lockout, while response time did not differ between lockout conditions.
cases.quote: We observed a higher sensitivity in the no lockout than lockout condition, t(84) = −2.60, p
cases.rationale: The two Results sentences report higher sensitivity in the no-lockout condition and no response-time difference. The selected span establishes the direction for sensitivity, and the full excerpt states the separate null response-time result.

cases.text: The sensitivity comparison produced p = .206, while the response-time comparison produced p = .011.
cases.quote: = .011, ηp² = .07, 95% CI [.01, .19] (see Fig. 3). Regarding response time, there
cases.rationale: The claim reverses the outcomes associated with the source-present p values: .011 belongs to sensitivity and .206 to response time. Numeric membership alone cannot detect the reassignment.

cases.text: Removing the lockout improved N-back sensitivity and made participants respond significantly faster.
cases.quote: We observed a higher sensitivity in the no lockout than lockout condition, t(84) = −2.60, p
cases.rationale: The sensitivity advantage is supported, but the additional speed improvement contradicts the explicitly reported absence of a response-time difference. The claim is false as a whole despite its partially supported first clause and relevant sensitivity anchor.

cases.text: N-back sensitivity was higher without a lockout, while response time did not differ between lockout conditions.

cases.rationale: The claim text is identical to outcomes_supported, but the selected literal span describes the foot-pedal response device. It provides no comparison of sensitivity or response time between lockout conditions.
